text: He is said ___ influential in the negotiations.
why: 'to be' is also correct (he is influential now / negotiations ongoing).

text: The committee recommended that the policy ___ immediately.
why: BrE accepts indicative after recommend ('is/was suspended'); British/American difference decides the answer.

text: The company’s decision was widely ___ as risky.
why: 'considered as' is widely used and accepted; options mix verb+preposition with a bare verb, so 'regarded'/'viewed' would also fit.

text: The data suggests that the trend is irreversible.
why: 'data suggests' (uncountable) is standard modern English; no real mistake.

text: Despite the fact that the evidence was clear, they rejected it.
why: Sentence has no mistake, yet a correct part is marked as the answer.

text: The number of complaints have risen sharply.
why: Fourth part is an empty string; also a B1/B2 agreement point.

text: The board decided to ___ ahead with the acquisition.
why: 'go ahead with' is B1, too easy for C1.

text: The company had to ___ back its expansion plans.
why: 'put back' (postpone) is also correct.

text: The negotiations finally ___ off after months of delay.
why: 'took off' (began to succeed / got going) also fits.

text: She managed to ___ around the bureaucratic obstacles.
why: 'go around' (bypass) is also acceptable; 'get around' is the most idiomatic and absent.

text: The evidence was considered highly ___. (RELIABLE)
why: 'reliable' itself fits ('highly reliable'); nothing forces the negative.

text: He was ___ of any wrongdoing.
why: 'absolved of any wrongdoing' is also correct.

text: The initiative, ___ ambitious, lacked funding.
why: 'although ambitious' is correct; 'however ambitious' is the odd one here; explanation misleading.

text: The committee is comprised of five members.
why: 'is comprised of' is in standard dictionaries and widely accepted; empty fourth part.

text: He was accused for falsifying the records.
why: Fourth part is an empty string.

text: The results corroborate with earlier studies.
why: Fourth part is an empty string.

text: She objected to the proposal to be delayed.
why: Awkward, ambiguous sentence ('the proposal to delay' vs 'the proposal being delayed'); empty fourth part.

text: The phenomenon is widely attributable for climate change.
why: 'widely attributable' is unnatural too and the meaning is confused (more than one problem).

text: The policy aims at reducing administrative burdens.
why: 'aims at reducing' is correct English; no mistake.

text: The team had to ___ up with an unexpected delay.
why: Answer wrong: 'put up with' is correct, 'come up with a delay' is not.

text: The project was ___ off due to funding problems.
why: Answer wrong: 'shelved off' is not English; 'put off' is correct.

text: They decided to ___ up the search after finding no evidence.
why: Answer wrong: 'give up' is correct, 'call up the search' is not; explanation talks about 'call off'.

text: The study provides strong ___ for the theory. (SUPPORT)
why: No word formation (answer = given word); trivial.

text: The decision was criticised for its lack of ___. (INCLUDE)
why: 'inclusiveness' and 'inclusion' are also correct and missing.

text: Not until the audit was completed did they realise the extent of the losses.
why: American spelling 'realize' missing from alternatives.

text: Her account of events did not ___ with the official record.
why: 'correspond to' is also correct.

text: The proposal was rejected on the ___ that it was too costly.
why: 'on the basis that' is also correct.

text: The evidence was ___ to suggest deliberate misconduct.
why: 'not enough' is also grammatical; explanation misleading.

text: The committee urged that the deadline ___ extended.
why: BrE accepts 'is extended' after urge that; British/American difference decides the answer.

text: The report raises concerns about the project’s viability.
why: No mistake; answer empty.

text: She was dissatisfied with the explanation provided.
why: No mistake; answer empty.

text: The findings are consistent to previous research.
why: Fourth part is an empty string.

text: He was charged with breach of contract.
why: No mistake; answer empty; empty fourth part.

text: The manager objected the proposed changes.
why: Fourth part is an empty string.

text: The auditors ___ into several irregular payments.
why: 'look into' is B1, too easy for C1.

text: The government plans to ___ out new safety standards.
why: Answer contradicts 'new' (phase out = stop using); 'bring out'/'put out' (introduce/publish) fit.

text: The team needs to ___ up with changing customer demands.
why: 'catch up with' also fits; B1 phrasal verb.

text: The proposal was viewed as economically ___. (SUSTAIN)
why: 'sustainable' also fits; nothing forces the negative.
